scenarios.title: Source ingestion & citation traceability
scenarios.intent: An analyst imports a primary source, cites its sections from model elements, and relies on the workspace to prove every citation resolves.

steps.label: Workspace parses from the canonical entrypoint
steps.expectation: domaiNN_NN.md resolves as entrypoint, models load, no parse issues

steps.label: All citations in a well-formed workspace resolve cleanly
steps.expectation: zero diagnostics — every `@` pointer resolves to a real file, heading and CSV row

steps.label: A heading citation parses into an addressable knowledge unit
steps.expectation: parses to a header unit at level 2 under sources/nn/

steps.label: Citation is structurally stable across a write-back cycle
steps.expectation: the pointer still resolves to the same heading after the agent writes it back

steps.label: Citation keeps its human-readable heading text across a write-back cycle
steps.expectation: a human wrote `@## Q4 Outlook`; after one save it should still read as `## Q4 Outlook`

steps.label: Cited section resolves to a concrete line range in the source
steps.expectation: the pointer maps to real text the user can read back, not just a string

steps.label: Element carrying the citation
Deleting the source file outside the app is reported, not silently ignored
steps.expectation: KU_DANGLING_FILE error naming the missing file

steps.label: Renaming a cited heading in the source surfaces a drift warning
steps.expectation: KU_UNKNOWN_SLUG — the file still exists but the cited unit moved

steps.label: Raw material under sources/original/ is refused as a citation target
steps.expectation: null — only normalized sources under sources/nn/ carry provenance

steps.label: A query string cannot stand in for a resolved citation
steps.expectation: QU_NOT_PROVENANCE error — queries must be resolved to pointers before being cited

scenarios.title: Modifying a model
scenarios.intent: A user adds a risk, edits it, renames an assumption other elements reference, and deletes a stale entry — expecting the file to stay coherent.

steps.label: Model loads with its elements addressable by concept
steps.expectation: concepts and elements are indexed the way the editor tree shows them

steps.label: Adding an element succeeds and lands under the right concept
steps.expectation: the new risk is present, no error

steps.label: A duplicate element name anywhere in the model is refused
steps.expectation: model-wide element name uniqueness (R-IE-02) is enforced

steps.label: Updating a field on an existing element succeeds
steps.expectation: no error; the field is written

steps.label: Editing a non-existent element fails loudly instead of silently creating one
steps.expectation: a clear error, and no phantom element

steps.label: Renaming an element also repoints the matrices that name it
steps.expectation: the matrix row label follows the rename — no dangling label

steps.label: The renamed element keeps its citations
steps.expectation: renaming must not drop the provenance attached to the element

steps.label: A misspelled concept name is refused rather than silently creating a new concept
steps.expectation: the template declares the legal concepts; `Rsiks` is not one of them

steps.label: Serialized model re-parses with the same element inventory
steps.expectation: a save/load cycle loses nothing

steps.label: Citations survive the save/load cycle in the spec-correct bracket form
steps.expectation: sources:: lines are written unquoted as `[a, b]`, matching what the reader expects
steps.actual:
[
  "sources:: [market-report-2026.md@## Q4 Outlook]",
  "sources:: [market-report-2026.md@## Cost Curve, unit-costs.csv@SKU-014]",
  "sources:: [market-report-2026.md@## Supplier Landscape]"
]

steps.label: Removing an element succeeds and it disappears from the model
steps.expectation: the element is gone

steps.label: An unknown operation is rejected and leaves the model untouched
steps.expectation: failed mutations are atomic — the document is byte-identical afterwards

steps.label: Fixture file on disk was never written
steps.actual: the simulation mutates in memory only; fixtures/acme stays pristine

scenarios.title: Save/load fidelity of shipped models
scenarios.intent: A user opens a shipped sample, changes nothing meaningful, saves — and expects a clean git diff.

steps.label: A no-op save leaves every shipped model byte-identical
steps.expectation: parse -> serialize is the identity on canonical, spec-conformant files

steps.label: Matrix axis labels survive a save
steps.expectation: a header reading `| Metrics  Variables |` must not become `| Row  Col |`

steps.label: Document section order survives a save
steps.expectation: the author chose the order of `# NN` sections; a save must not reshuffle it

steps.label: Bracketed list values survive a save
steps.expectation: `tags:: [a, b]` must not silently become `tags:: a, b`

steps.label: Second-pass stability (is the canonical form at least a fixed point?)
The canonical form is at least stable after the first save
steps.expectation: once degraded, further saves produce no further drift (bounded damage)

scenarios.title: Template-authoring gate (level 2 vs level 3)
scenarios.intent: An agent tries to extend the schema from inside a user model; the gate must hold.

steps.label: Level-3 model refuses `add_concept`
steps.expectation: schema-authoring ops are gated to level-2 documents

steps.label: Level-3 model refuses `add_field`
steps.expectation: schema-authoring ops are gated to level-2 documents

steps.label: Level-3 model refuses `set_marker`
steps.expectation: schema-authoring ops are gated to level-2 documents

steps.label: The same op succeeds on a level-2 template
steps.expectation: the gate discriminates by level, it does not simply forbid the op

steps.label: A level-3 model declaring inline schema is rejected by validation
steps.expectation: an error naming the illegal frontmatter key

steps.label: What a level-3 model looks like after a refused mutation
steps.expectation: no `# NN Concept Definition` section should have appeared
steps.actual: # NN Analysis | # NN Assumptions | # NN Risks | # NN Keys | # NN matrices: assumptions-risks matrix

scenarios.title: Tabular source ingestion & row-level citations
scenarios.intent: An analyst imports a cost table and cites one SKU row from a model assumption.

steps.label: The imported table parses with a usable key column
steps.expectation: columns and three data rows

steps.label: A row citation parses as a row unit, not a heading
steps.expectation: the `.csv` extension selects the row grammar automatically

steps.label: A valid row citation produces no diagnostics
steps.expectation: SKU-014 exists in the table, so nothing to report

steps.label: Deleting the cited row upstream is reported
steps.expectation: KU_UNKNOWN_ROW error — the citation no longer resolves

steps.label: Duplicate keys in the source table are reported once, not per citation
steps.expectation: exactly one KU_DUPLICATE_KEY for the file

steps.label: A line-range citation is refused (line numbers are not stable provenance)
steps.expectation: null — provenance addresses named units, never line offsets

scenarios.title: Workspace manifest reconciliation
scenarios.intent: A user adds a model file by hand and expects the workspace index to notice — without losing their own edits.

steps.label: Reconciling an already-correct manifest changes nothing
steps.expectation: no changes and a byte-identical document (the documented round-trip guarantee)

steps.label: A newly added model file is registered in the manifest
steps.expectation: one `added` change and a new `## NN Models:` entry

steps.label: Tool-written entries are explicitly marked as tool-owned
steps.expectation: the ownership marker <!-- nn:auto --> appears on the generated entry

steps.label: A human-owned entry whose file is gone is reported, never silently deleted
steps.expectation: the tool reports it rather than editing something it does not own

steps.label: validateWorkspaceReferences requires a WorkspaceIndex the type surface does not make obvious
steps.actual: calling it with the index omitted throws a raw TypeError on `index.nodeSchema` rather than a named error

steps.label: Workspace-wide reference validation runs clean on a coherent workspace
steps.expectation: no dangling cross-model references

steps.label: Models the workspace scan discovered

scenarios.title: Opening the shipped sample workspace
scenarios.intent: A new user opens the workspace we ship. Everything they see on day one is what this scenario measures.

steps.label: The shipped workspace parses without issues
steps.expectation: all sample models load with no error or warning issues — this is the first thing a new user sees

steps.label: Every shipped sample passes document hygiene with no errors
steps.expectation: zero hygiene errors across the eleven samples

steps.label: Every citation in the shipped workspace resolves
steps.expectation: a new user opening the sample sees no broken provenance

steps.label: The shipped workspace contains the sources its models cite
steps.expectation: source traceability is the headline capability — the demo must demonstrate it

steps.label: Every artifact the shipped workspace declares actually exists
steps.expectation: the workspace must not advertise an artifact it does not ship

steps.label: A field named `source` that is declared as a content path is not treated as a citation
steps.expectation: the Citation vocabulary should key on the declared field TYPE, not on the field NAME

scenarios.title: Consuming innfo-core from plain Node
scenarios.intent: An integrator runs `npm i @cognnitive/innfo-core` and writes `import { parseKnowledge } from ...` in a Node script.

steps.label: The published package imports under plain Node ESM
steps.expectation: package.json declares "type":"module" and "main":"./dist/index.js" — Node must be able to load it

steps.label: Once bundled, the public API surface is complete and usable
steps.expectation: the API itself is fine — only the module format blocks plain-Node consumption

steps.label: Why every existing consumer hides this
steps.actual: innfo-editor resolves through Vite, the test suites through Vitest, innfo-mcp through tsup — all bundlers, all of which tolerate extensionless directory imports that Node rejects.
